object_description: large, symmetrically organised three-storey volume standing alone with a veranda entrance
design_condition: the large volume stands alone in the complex close to the road, taking on the scale of the neighbourhood and staggering with the slope, though its large footprint severely restricts the surrounding usable area

positive: The height of the building takes on the scale of the neighbourhood
The slope-following staggering achieves a successful integration
The proposal is characterised by a clear volume, organised on the visible above-ground footprint even in the basement
The autonomous setting suggests special consideration for the listed school building
The distance to the neighbouring school building is maintained
The frontage is reinforced by the veranda as a symmetrical entrance to the complex
A spacious school square spans from the schoolyard to the existing gymnasium wing as the central outdoor element
A staircase leads to the canteen outdoor area with a visual connection to the neighbouring school
The all-weather pitches on two levels are intended as a link and synergy between the two schools
The positioning of canteen and multi-purpose rooms with outdoor areas inviting communal use is appreciated
The spaciousness of the interconnecting rooms is welcome
The indoor swimming pool is prominent and well lit
The rhythmic concrete element facade and folded roof recall the existing school buildings and the expression is convincing
negative: The occupied floor area severely restricts the usable surrounding area
The land consumption appears very large overall in the existing context
Seen as a whole the new building has little relationship with the existing building
The downdraughts are significantly influenced by the size of the building
An inaccessible rear side is proposed towards one street
Accessing all uses via the main entrance produces an operationally sophisticated mix of uses
It is questionable whether the ball catcher constructions restrict the line of sight
The organisation is dominated by the symmetry and does not seem very efficient, with two entrances per unit
Access routes via the cascading staircases are very long and not very intuitive
Routing everyday school access past the indoor swimming pool is viewed critically
The kitchen on the opposite side of the building is impractical
The large upper floors with a circular corridor and only one lift produce long routes and prove very uneconomical
The veranda is not understood in connection with the quite successful side facades
The urban positioning makes little reference to the existing complex
The symmetry, access typology and functional arrangement are not convincing
